metadata.description: Comprehensive disease treatment protocols for major crop diseases in India
metadata.source: ICAR, Plant Pathology Research Institutes, and Agricultural Universities
metadata.coverage: Major fungal, bacterial, viral, and pest-related diseases

fungal.common_conditions: High humidity, moderate temperature, poor air circulation
fungal.prevention: Proper spacing, fungicide sprays, resistant varieties

bacterial.common_conditions: Warm, humid weather, wounds, contaminated tools

viral.common_conditions: Vector insects, contaminated tools, infected seeds
viral.prevention: Vector control, virus-free seeds, roguing infected plants

pest.description: Damage caused by insects and pests
pest.common_conditions: Favorable weather, monoculture, lack of natural enemies
pest.prevention: IPM practices, biological control, resistant varieties

symptoms: Diamond-shaped lesions on leaves with gray centers and brown margins
Neck rot causing panicle breakage
Node blast causing stem breakage

favorable_conditions.weather: Cloudy, humid conditions with intermittent rain

immediate_action: Remove and destroy infected plant debris
Improve field drainage to reduce humidity

fungicides.name: Tricyclazole 75% WP
fungicides.application: Spray at tillering and panicle initiation stage

cultural_practices: Use resistant varieties like Pusa Basmati-1121, PR-126

prevention.seed_treatment: Carbendazim 2 g/kg seed or hot water treatment at 52°C for 10 minutes
prevention.field_preparation: Deep plowing and removal of crop residues
prevention.water_management: Avoid water stagnation, maintain 2-3 cm water level

rice_blast.economic_threshold: 5% leaf area affected or 1-2 lesions per leaf

symptoms: Water-soaked lesions starting from leaf tips or margins
Yellow to straw-colored stripes with wavy margins
Bacterial ooze visible in early morning
Kresek symptom in severe cases (wilting of entire plant)

immediate_action: Remove infected plants and burn them
biological_control: Pseudomonas fluorescens seed treatment (10 g/kg seed)
Bacillus subtilis foliar spray (5 g/L water)
cultural_practices: Use resistant varieties like Improved Samba Mahsuri, DRR Dhan 42

prevention.seed_treatment: Hot water treatment at 52-54°C for 30 minutes
prevention.field_sanitation: Remove crop residues and volunteer plants
prevention.water_management: Avoid overflow irrigation from infected fields

symptoms: Water-soaked dark green to brown lesions on leaves
White fungal growth on undersurface of leaves
Rapid spread during cool, humid weather
Tuber rot with reddish-brown discoloration

favorable_conditions.weather: Cool, wet conditions with fog or dew

cultural_practices: Hill up soil around plants to protect tubers

prevention.seed_treatment: Treat seed tubers with Mancozeb 3 g/L water
prevention.field_preparation: Ensure good drainage and avoid waterlogging
prevention.monitoring: Regular field inspection during cool, humid weather

late_blight.economic_threshold: 1% plants affected or first appearance of symptoms

symptoms: Circular holes in leaves and bolls
Caterpillars feeding inside bolls
Frass (insect excrement) near feeding sites
Damaged squares and flowers dropping

favorable_conditions.weather: Warm, dry conditions during flowering stage

immediate_action: Hand-pick and destroy egg masses and young larvae
cultural_practices: Deep summer plowing to expose pupae

prevention.monitoring: Install pheromone traps @ 5/ha from 45 days after sowing
prevention.economic_threshold: 2 larvae per plant or 10% damaged bolls
prevention.resistant_varieties: Use Bt cotton varieties where approved

wheat_rust.scientific_name: Puccinia triticina (leaf rust), Puccinia graminis (stem rust)
symptoms: Orange to reddish-brown pustules on leaves (leaf rust)
Dark reddish-brown pustules on stems (stem rust)
Yellow to orange pustules on leaves (stripe rust)
Premature leaf senescence and reduced grain filling

immediate_action: Apply fungicide spray at first appearance
Remove alternate hosts (barberry for stem rust)
Monitor weather conditions for disease development
cultural_practices: Use resistant varieties like HD-2967, WH-542, DBW-88
Avoid late sowing to escape disease pressure

prevention.field_sanitation: Remove volunteer plants and crop residues

wheat_rust.economic_threshold: 5-10% leaf area affected at flag leaf stage

symptoms: Yellow patches on upper leaf surface
Grayish-white fuzzy growth on undersurface
Leaf curling and distortion
Premature leaf drop and stunted growth

favorable_conditions.weather: Cool, wet conditions with poor air circulation

immediate_action: Remove infected leaves and destroy them
cultural_practices: Proper plant spacing for air circulation
Mulching to reduce soil moisture evaporation

prevention.field_management: Ensure good drainage and avoid waterlogging

principles: Use of resistant varieties as first line of defense
Judicious use of chemicals as last resort
monitoring_tools: Yellow sticky traps for flying insects
